question: Acid changes the colour of blue litmus to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is red.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acids turn blue litmus paper red because acids furnish hydrogen ions (H⁺) in aqueous solution, which react with the blue litmus dye and change its colour to red. (अम्ल — नीले लिटमस को लाल करता है)

 

• Litmus is a natural pH indicator extracted from lichens; it is neutral (purple) in pure form, turns red in acidic solutions (pH < 7) and blue in basic/alkaline solutions (pH > 7).

 

• Common acids such as hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid, and citric acid (found in lemon juice) all turn blue litmus red.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Conversely, bases turn red litmus paper blue; neutral substances such as pure water do not change the colour of litmus.

 

• Other common indicators include phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base) and methyl orange (red in acid, yellow in base).

 

NOTE

 

• yellow (Option 1): Not a colour change associated with the litmus test.

 

• pink (Option 3): This is the colour phenolphthalein turns in a basic solution, not the litmus colour change.

 

• orange (Option 4): Not a colour change associated with the litmus test.

question: Which of the following hills and their region are correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Javadi hills – Eastern ghats.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Javadi Hills are located in Tamil Nadu (Vellore and Tiruvannamalai districts) and form part of the Eastern Ghats. (जावडी पहाड़ियाँ — पूर्वी घाट)

 

• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous, eroded range running along India's eastern coast; important hill ranges within it include the Javadi, Shevaroy, Palkonda and Nallamala hills.

 

• The Patkai and Mizo hills lie in North-East India, forming part of the Purvanchal ranges, and are unrelated to either the Western or Eastern Ghats.

 

• The Shevaroy Hills (around Yercaud, Salem district, Tamil Nadu) are also part of the Eastern Ghats, not the Western Ghats as stated in Option 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Western Ghats run along India's west coast through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, and include the Nilgiri, Anamalai and Cardamom hills; they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a biodiversity hotspot.

 

NOTE

 

• Patkai hills – Western ghats (Option 1): Incorrect; the Patkai hills are part of the North-Eastern hill ranges (Purvanchal), not the Western Ghats.

 

• Mizo hills – Eastern ghats (Option 2): Incorrect; the Mizo hills are also part of the North-Eastern hill ranges, not the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Shevaroy hills – Western ghats (Option 3): Incorrect; the Shevaroy hills belong to the Eastern Ghats, not the Western Ghats.

question: Under the Constitution of India, the Constitutional Head of the Executive of the Union is the _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 53 of the Constitution vests the executive power of the Union in the President, who is the constitutional (nominal) head of the Executive. (राष्ट्रपति — संघ की कार्यपालिका का संवैधानिक प्रधान)

 

• As per Article 74, the real executive power is exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, since India follows a parliamentary system of government.

 

• The President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, a position made explicitly binding by the 42nd and 44th Constitutional Amendments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the state level, the Governor similarly acts as the constitutional (nominal) head of the state executive, with real power resting with the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers.

 

NOTE

 

• Prime Minister (Option 1): He/she is the real executive head, not the constitutional/nominal head.

 

• Supreme Court Chief Justice (Option 3): Heads the judiciary, not the executive.

 

• Speaker of the Rajya Sabha (Option 4): This post does not exist; the presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha is the Chairman, an office held ex-officio by the Vice-President of India. The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha.

question: Kathak dancer, Sitara Devi was awarded which of the following awards in 1973?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sitara Devi, popularly known as the "Kathak Queen," was one of the most celebrated exponents of Kathak dance in India and was awarded the Padma Shri in 1973. (सितारा देवी — पद्म श्री 1973)

 

• She had earlier received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1969 for her contribution to Kathak.

 

• She later famously declined the Padma Bhushan, calling it "an insult, not an honour," and stated she would accept nothing less than the Bharat Ratna for her contribution to the art form.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sitara Devi also received the Kalidas Samman in 1995 and performed in several Hindi films during her career.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 1): She was never conferred this award.

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 2): She was offered this award later in her career but declined it.

 

• Sangam Kala (Option 3): Not a recognised Indian civilian or cultural award.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the recognition of the right to education as a Fundamental Right?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 21 A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, guarantees free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years as a Fundamental Right. (अनुच्छेद 21A — शिक्षा का मौलिक अधिकार)

 

• This amendment led to the enactment of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

 

• Before this amendment, education was only a Directive Principle of State Policy under Article 45; the 86th Amendment elevated it to the status of a Fundamental Right.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21, the parent provision, guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, from which Article 21A was carved out.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 300 A (Option 1): Deals with the Right to Property, a legal right (not a Fundamental Right) after the 44th Amendment.

 

• Article 20 (Option 2): Provides protection in respect of conviction for offences.

 

• Article 33 (Option 3): Empowers Parliament to modify the application of Fundamental Rights to members of the armed forces and police.

question: During the period between 1950 and 1990, the proportion of GDP contributed by agriculture significantly ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is declined.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Between 1950-51 and 1990-91, the share of agriculture in India's GDP declined significantly, from around 55% to about 29-30%, reflecting the structural transformation of the economy. (कृषि का जीडीपी में योगदान — में गिरावट)

 

• This decline continued after the 1991 economic reforms, with agriculture's share of GDP falling further to around 15-18% in later decades, even as it continued to employ a large share of the workforce.

 

• This pattern — a falling share of the primary sector in GDP alongside a rising share of industry and services — is typical of structural economic development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The mismatch between agriculture's shrinking share in GDP and its still-large share of employment is often cited as a sign of disguised unemployment in the Indian agricultural sector.

 

NOTE

 

• doubled (Option 1), remained constant (Option 2) and increased (Option 3): All contradict the well-documented long-term decline in agriculture's share of India's GDP during this period.

question: What is the product of a reaction of calcium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium hydrogen carbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) reacts with water and carbon dioxide, it forms soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate (calcium bicarbonate), Ca(HCO₃)₂: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂. (कैल्सियम हाइड्रोजन कार्बोनेट — अस्थायी कठोरता का कारण)

 

• This reaction is responsible for the temporary hardness of water and also explains the formation of stalactites and stalagmites in limestone caves as rainwater carrying dissolved CO₂ dissolves and later re-deposits limestone.

 

• On boiling, Ca(HCO₃)₂ decomposes back into insoluble CaCO₃, releasing CO₂ and H₂O — which is why boiling removes temporary hardness from water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pure CaCO₃ is insoluble in water; this reaction converts it into the soluble bicarbonate form, which is how limestone gets gradually eroded by carbonic acid in rainwater.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcium oxide (Option 1): Formed by strongly heating limestone (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂), a different reaction (thermal decomposition).

 

• Calcium hydroxide (Option 2): Formed when calcium oxide reacts with water (slaking of lime), not from this reaction.

 

• Hydrochloric acid (Option 3): Not a product of this reaction; it is unrelated.

question: Fa Xian began his journey back home from which of the following Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fa Xian (Faxian), the Chinese Buddhist monk-traveller, visited India during the reign of the Gupta ruler Chandragupta II and began his sea journey back to China from the port of Tamralipti, located in present-day Bengal. (फाह्यान — तामलिप्ति, बंगाल)

 

• He spent about six years in India, studying Buddhist texts and visiting important sites, before sailing home via Sri Lanka.

 

• His travel account, known as the "Fo-Kwo-Ki" (Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms), is an important historical source on the Gupta period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later Chinese pilgrims to India include Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang), who visited during the reign of Harshavardhana, and Yijing (I-tsing).

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1), Maharashtra (Option 2) and Odisha (Option 4): Fa Xian travelled through parts of India including Bihar (Pataliputra), but the port from which he began his return sea voyage was Tamralipti in Bengal, not any of these states.

question: Gross primary deficit can be expressed as ______.
option_1: Gross fiscal deficit – Net interest liabilities
option_3: Gross fiscal deficit + Net interest liabilities
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross fiscal deficit – Net interest liabilities.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit − Net Interest Liabilities (interest payments). It measures the government's borrowing requirement excluding interest obligations on past debt. (प्राथमिक घाटा — राजकोषीय घाटा घटा ब्याज देयताएँ)

 

• Fiscal deficit itself is defined as Total expenditure − Total receipts excluding borrowings.

 

• The primary deficit isolates the government's *current* borrowing requirement from the burden of past borrowings, making it a useful indicator of the present fiscal stance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts, and it measures the shortfall of revenue receipts over revenue expenditure.

 

• The Effective Revenue Deficit further excludes grants given for the creation of capital assets from the revenue deficit.

 

NOTE

 

• Capital expenditure – Revenue deficit (Option 2): Not the correct formula for primary deficit.

 

• Gross fiscal deficit + Net interest liabilities (Option 3): Reverses the correct operation (subtraction, not addition).

 

• Revenue deficit + Capital expenditure (Option 4): Not related to the definition of primary deficit.

question: The news print sector in our country is governed by which order from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newsprint Control Order, 2004.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The newsprint sector in India is governed by the Newsprint Control Order, 2004, issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, which regulates the import, movement, and allocation of newsprint used by registered publications. (न्यूज़प्रिंट नियंत्रण आदेश 2004 — समाचार पत्र क्षेत्र)

 

• It replaced the earlier Newsprint Control Order of 1962, which had governed the sector for several decades.

 

• The Order aims to ensure availability of newsprint at reasonable rates to registered newspapers and periodicals in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newsprint imported for actual use by registered newspaper publications is exempt from customs duty under the relevant import policy provisions.

 

NOTE

 

• National Print Control Order, 2001 (Option 1), News Print Commission Order, 2006 (Option 3) and National Press Control Order, 2003 (Option 4): None of these are genuine government orders; they are not the instrument governing India's newsprint sector.

question: Which element of group 13 is a soft metal with a low melting point (303K) and is widely used in doping semiconductors and producing solid-state devices such as transistors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gallium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gallium (Ga), a group 13 element, is a soft metal with an unusually low melting point of about 29.76°C (≈303 K) — it can even melt in the palm of a hand. (गैलियम — अर्धचालकों में डोपिंग हेतु प्रयुक्त)

 

• It is widely used for doping semiconductors and in compounds such as gallium arsenide (GaAs) for making solid-state devices like transistors, LEDs and laser diodes.

 

• Gallium also has a very high boiling point (~2400°C), giving it one of the largest liquid ranges of any element.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gallium was discovered by Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran in 1875; its existence and properties had been predicted earlier by Mendeleev, who called it "eka-aluminium."

 

NOTE

 

• Aluminium (Option 1): A group 13 metal, but with a much higher melting point (~660°C) and not primarily used as a semiconductor dopant in this manner.

 

• Boron (Option 2): A group 13 metalloid with a very high melting point (~2076°C), unlike a soft, low-melting metal.

 

• Thallium (Option 3): A group 13 metal, but its melting point is about 304°C (≈577 K), far higher than the 303 K mentioned in the question, and it is toxic rather than being the standard semiconductor dopant.

question: What type of isomerism exists in compounds containing two or more complexes, each of which contains a different set of ligands that can in principle be replaced with a ligand of the other complex?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coordination isomerism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Coordination isomerism occurs in coordination compounds made up of both a cationic and an anionic complex ion, where the two (or more) metal centres can exchange ligands between their respective coordination spheres. (उपसहसंयोजक समावयवता — Coordination isomerism)

 

• A classic example is [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆] and [Cr(NH₃)₆][Co(CN)₆] — coordination isomers in which the NH₃ and CN⁻ ligands are distributed differently between the Co and Cr centres.

 

• It is a type of structural (constitutional) isomerism specific to compounds containing more than one metal-ligand complex.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Linkage isomerism arises from an ambidentate ligand (e.g., NO₂⁻/ONO⁻, SCN⁻/NCS⁻) binding through different donor atoms.

 

NOTE

 

• Solvate Isomerism (Option 2): Arises when a solvent molecule (commonly water) occupies a position inside vs. outside the coordination sphere, not from ligand exchange between two complexes.

 

• Linkage isomerism (Option 3): Arises from an ambidentate ligand binding through different donor atoms, not from ligand exchange between complexes.

 

• Ionisation isomerism (Option 4): Arises when a counter ion and a ligand within the coordination sphere exchange places.

question: “Radcliffe line” separate India with which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Radcliffe Line, drawn by British lawyer Sir Cyril Radcliffe, is the boundary demarcation line between India and Pakistan, covering the partition of the provinces of Punjab and Bengal. (रैडक्लिफ रेखा — भारत-पाकिस्तान सीमा)

 

• It was published on 17 August 1947, two days after independence, forming the basis of the partition of British India into India and Pakistan.

 

• The line runs for about 3,323 km, and today forms both the India-Pakistan border and the India-Bangladesh border (Bangladesh was then East Pakistan, part of Pakistan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The India-China border is delimited (in a disputed manner) by the McMahon Line in the east and the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

 

NOTE

 

• China (Option 1): India's boundary with China is associated with the McMahon Line/LAC, not the Radcliffe Line.

 

• Nepal (Option 3): India shares an open border with Nepal, unrelated to the Radcliffe Line.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 4): In 1947, present-day Bangladesh was part of Pakistan (East Pakistan); the Radcliffe Line was drawn to separate India from Pakistan as a whole, so Pakistan is the standard textbook answer.

question: Which of the following rocks is formed by the cooling and crystallisation of magma?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Granite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Granite is an intrusive igneous rock, formed by the slow cooling and crystallisation of magma deep within the Earth's crust, giving it a characteristic coarse-grained texture. (ग्रेनाइट — मैग्मा के ठंडा होने से निर्मित)

 

• Igneous rocks are broadly classified as intrusive (formed inside the crust, e.g., granite) or extrusive (formed on the surface from lava, e.g., basalt).

 

• Granite is composed mainly of quartz, feldspar and mica.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Basalt is a common extrusive igneous rock, formed from rapidly cooling lava, and forms features like the Deccan Traps in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Chalk (Option 2): A soft, fine-grained sedimentary rock formed from calcium carbonate deposits (remains of marine organisms).

 

• Coal (Option 3): An organic sedimentary rock formed from the compression of ancient plant matter, not from magma.

 

• Shell (Option 4): Referring to shale/shell-derived sedimentary material — formed from compacted clay, mud and organic remains, not from cooling magma.

question: In July 2022, who was appointed as the deputy election commissioner of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R K Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• R K Gupta, a senior officer, was appointed as a Deputy Election Commissioner of India in July 2022. (आर के गुप्ता — उप निर्वाचन आयुक्त)

 

• The Election Commission of India (ECI), established under Article 324 of the Constitution, is headed by the Chief Election Commissioner along with two Election Commissioners, and is assisted by senior Deputy Election Commissioners.

 

• The ECI is responsible for administering elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950, which is now observed as National Voters' Day.

 

NOTE

 

• Asit Rath (Option 2), Suranjan Das (Option 3) and R. Dinesh (Option 4): These names are distractors not linked to this July 2022 Deputy Election Commissioner appointment.

question: Who among the following personalities is an exponent of Kathak dance in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prerna Shrimali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prerna Shrimali is a well-known exponent of Kathak dance in India, associated with the Jaipur Gharana tradition of Kathak. (प्रेरणा श्रीमाली — कथक नृत्यांगना)

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in North India, characterised by intricate rhythmic footwork, spins (chakkars), and storytelling through expressive gestures.

 

• Other well-known Kathak exponents include Pandit Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi and Shovana Narayan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The major gharanas (schools) of Kathak are the Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas.

 

NOTE

 

• Usha Uthup (Option 2): A well-known Indian playback and pop singer, not a Kathak dancer.

 

• Suman Kalyanpur (Option 3): A veteran Indian playback singer, not a Kathak dancer.

 

• Monali Thakur (Option 4): A contemporary Indian playback singer, not a Kathak dancer.

question: Who has been appointed as the chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nidhi Chibber.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nidhi Chibber, an IAS officer, was appointed as the Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in May 2022. (निधि छिब्बर — सीबीएसई अध्यक्ष)

 

• CBSE is the apex national board for school education, functioning under the Union Ministry of Education, and conducts board examinations for Classes 10 and 12 across affiliated schools in India and abroad.

 

• CBSE was established in 1962 and is headquartered in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• CBSE also conducts national-level entrance examinations, such as being historically associated with NEET and JEE (Main) administration.

 

NOTE

 

• Nalin Negi (Option 1), Satyendra Prakash (Option 3) and Ashish Jha (Option 4): These names are distractors not linked to this May 2022 CBSE chairperson appointment.

question: Which of the following Gharanas does Padma Bhushan Kishori Amonkar belong to?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur - Atrauli.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kishori Amonkar, a celebrated Hindustani classical vocalist, belonged to the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana. (जयपुर-अतरौली घराना — किशोरी अमोणकर)

 

• She was trained by her mother, Mogubai Kurdikar, herself a disciple of Ustad Alladiya Khan, the founder of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana.

 

• Kishori Amonkar was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1987) and later the Padma Vibhushan (2002) for her contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• She was also conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1985) and is remembered for her distinctive, emotive style of khayal singing.

 

NOTE

 

• Gwalior (Option 1): The oldest khayal gharana, associated with vocalists such as Omkarnath Thakur.

 

• Kirana (Option 2): Associated with vocalists such as Bhimsen Joshi and Gangubai Hangal.

 

• Patiala (Option 3): Associated with vocalists such as Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

question: Who among the following was the founder of Visva-Bharati University?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindranath Tagore founded Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan, West Bengal, formally established in 1921, growing out of an earlier experimental school he had started there in 1901. (रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर — विश्व-भारती विश्वविद्यालय)

 

• Tagore was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913), for his collection of poems "Gitanjali."

 

• Visva-Bharati was declared a Central University and an Institution of National Importance by an Act of Parliament in 1951.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tagore also composed the national anthems of both India ("Jana Gana Mana") and Bangladesh ("Amar Shonar Bangla").

 

NOTE

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 1): Founded Banaras Hindu University (BHU).

 

• Lala Hardayal (Option 2): A revolutionary who founded the Ghadar Party in the USA.

 

• Swami Vivekananda (Option 3): Founded the Ramakrishna Mission, not Visva-Bharati University.

question: Which state government launched the Mission Bhumiputra in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Assam government launched "Mission Bhumiputra" in August 2022, an online portal for the digitised issuance of caste certificates (ST/SC/OBC/MOBC) to indigenous residents of the state. (मिशन भूमिपुत्र — असम सरकार)

 

• It was launched by Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, aiming to simplify and speed up the caste-certificate application process for students and citizens.

 

• The mission is aimed at reducing bureaucratic delays and preventing fraudulent certificate issuance through digitisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Assam government has also launched other welfare schemes such as Orunodoi, a direct benefit transfer scheme for economically weaker families.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagaland (Option 1), Bihar (Option 2) and Sikkim (Option 3): None of these state governments launched Mission Bhumiputra; it is specific to Assam.

question: In the ____________, Sarojini Naidu persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to allow women to join the movement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salt Satyagraha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March, 1930), Sarojini Naidu persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to allow women to actively participate in the movement, and she herself later led the raid on the Dharasana Salt Works after Gandhi's arrest. (सरोजिनी नायडू — नमक सत्याग्रह)

 

• Gandhi had initially planned the Dandi March with only male volunteers, but relented after Naidu's persuasion, and women went on to play a major role in the subsequent civil disobedience, including breaking the salt law at various depots.

 

• Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (1925) and the first woman Governor of independent India (United Provinces, 1947).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Salt Satyagraha began with Gandhi's Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (240 miles), starting on 12 March 1930, to break the British salt monopoly.

 

NOTE

 

• Quit India Movement (Option 1): Launched in 1942; unrelated to this specific 1930 incident.

 

• Champaran Satyagraha (Option 2): Gandhi's first satyagraha in India (1917), concerning indigo farmers in Bihar.

 

• Non-Cooperation Movement (Option 4): Launched in 1920-22; unrelated to this specific incident of persuading Gandhi to include women in the Salt Satyagraha.

question: The World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2022 was held in_______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dubai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 World Para Athletics Grand Prix season opened in Dubai, UAE. (दुबई — विश्व पैरा एथलेटिक्स ग्रां प्री 2022)

 

• The World Para Athletics Grand Prix is a series of international para-athletics competitions organised under the International Paralympic Committee (IPC), held across multiple legs in different cities each year.

 

• Top para-athletes, including multiple Paralympic and world champions, competed at the 2022 Dubai leg.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other legs of the World Para Athletics Grand Prix have been hosted in cities such as Nottwil (Switzerland) and Marrakech (Morocco).

 

NOTE

 

• Sharjah (Option 1), Istanbul (Option 2) and Doha (Option 4): These cities have hosted other international para-sport or athletics events, but not the 2022 World Para Athletics Grand Prix in question here.

question: Rajkumar Singhajit Singh, a leading exponent and guru of Indian classical Manipuri dance form, was awarded which of the following Indian civilian honours in 1986?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajkumar Singhajit Singh, a renowned exponent and guru of Manipuri dance, was awarded the Padma Shri in 1986 for his contribution to Indian classical dance. (राजकुमार सिंहजीत सिंह — पद्म श्री 1986)

 

• He headed the Manipuri Dance Section at Triveni Kala Sangam, New Delhi, from 1954 and later founded the Triveni Ballet in 1962 as its Director and Principal Dancer.

 

• He was also honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1984) and later the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (2011), the Akademi's highest honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Along with his wife, Charu Sija Mathur, he established the Manipuri Nrityashram, a dedicated Manipuri dance training institution in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Padma Bhushan (Option 1) and Padma Vibhushan (Option 4): Higher-tier civilian honours; not the award he received in 1986.

 

• Bharat Ratna (Option 3): India's highest civilian award; he was not conferred this honour.

question: Subsidiary alliance treaty was imposed on Awadh in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1801.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Subsidiary Alliance was imposed on the Nawab of Awadh (Oudh), Saadat Ali Khan II, in 1801 by Governor-General Lord Wellesley. (अवध पर सहायक संधि — 1801)

 

• Under this treaty, Awadh ceded roughly half of its territory — including Rohilkhand and the Lower Doab — to the British East India Company in exchange for the stationing of British troops for its "protection."

 

• The Subsidiary Alliance system was devised by Lord Wellesley as a method of bringing Indian princely states under indirect British political and military control.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Awadh was ultimately fully annexed by the British under Lord Dalhousie in 1856, on the pretext of misgovernance, becoming one of the immediate triggers for the Revolt of 1857.

 

NOTE

 

• 1802 (Option 1), 1803 (Option 2) and 1804 (Option 4): Incorrect years; the Subsidiary Alliance treaty with Awadh was signed in 1801.
